name: Taï National Park
region: Cavally, San Pedro and Nawa regions, south-west · Côte d'Ivoire
subtitle: Taï National Park is a forest reserve in south-west Côte d'Ivoire between the Cavally and Sassandra rivers, declared a national park in 1972 and inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1982.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: The largest remaining forest in West Africa and the last large island of original Upper Guinean forest

facts.label: Location
facts.value: South-west Côte d'Ivoire, between the Cavally River (border with Liberia) and the Sassandra River

facts.label: National park status
facts.value: Declared a National Park in 1972 (350,000 ha at that time)

facts.label: Earlier protection
facts.value: Declared a Forest Reserve and Wildlife Refuge in 1926 (560,300 ha)

facts.label: World Heritage
facts.value: Inscribed as a Natural World Heritage Site in 1982 under criteria vii and x

facts.label: Area (datasheet)
facts.value: Core zone 330,000 ha and buffer zone 20,000 ha; with the N'zo Reserve added, a total of 536,000 ha

facts.label: Area (2025)
facts.value: About 5,360 km², across the San Pedro, Nawa and Cavally regions, with an estimated 98.4% forest cover

facts.label: Management
facts.value: Managed by the OIPR; achieved 74% performance in implementing 2025 activities

facts.label: Green List
facts.value: Inscribed on the IUCN Green List

facts.label: Species
facts.value: 140 mammal species, including 47 of the 54 large mammals known in the Guinean rain forest

facts.label: Peoples of the forest region
facts.value: Original tribes were the Guéré and Oubi, who did not eat chimpanzees for totemic reasons

facts.label: Threats (datasheet)
facts.value: Civil unrest and encroachment by refugees aggravated poaching, tree clearance for farms, gold-mining and logging

facts.label: Enforcement 2021-2023
facts.value: 301 people arrested and handed to the courts; 235 firm sentences and 30 suspended

parts.text: Taï National Park is a forest reserve in south-west Côte d'Ivoire between the Cavally and Sassandra rivers, declared a national park in 1972 and inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1982. It is described as the largest remaining forest in West Africa. Managed by the Office ivoirien des parcs et réserves (OIPR), it is currently reported at about 5,360 km² with 98.4% forest cover, while gold-mining and poaching remain pressures.
